chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Bukayr, who said:
I testify regarding Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that I heard him saying: 'The absentee divorces by the new moons and the months.'
ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period (iddah) calculated for a divorced woman whose husband is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that for an absent husband, the 'iddah is determined by the passage of lunar months (shuhur) rather than menstrual cycles, a ruling derived from the principle of ease in cases of uncertainty. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach to resolving practical ambiguities in family law when the spouse is unavailable, ensuring the waiting period is calculated objectively based on time elapsed.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara, from Bukeyr who said,
‘I hereby testify upon Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The absentee should divorce by the (counting of the) new-moons and the months’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah from ibn Bukayr who has said the following: “I can testify that I heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘A man absent from his wife can divorce her by counting new moons and months.’”
